name: Bullshit
description: Bullshit (also known as BS, Cheat, or I Doubt It) is a shedding card game where players play cards face down and claim they are of a specific rank. Other players can challenge (call 'bullshit', 'cheat', or 'I doubt it') if they think the player is lying. If caught lying, the player takes the pile; if the challenge is wrong, the challenger takes the pile.

history.origins: Traditional shedding and bluffing game associated with Britain (Cheat) and the United States (Bullshit), documented in the 20th century. Multiple similar games exist worldwide under various names. The core mechanic of playing face-down cards with challenges appears in many cultures.
timeline: Traditional origins: Similar games played for generations worldwide
20th century: Documented in card game books under various names
Modern Era: One of the most popular casual card games globally
Cultural spread: Different versions in different countries (I Doubt It, BS, Cheat, Bluff, etc.)
history.cultural: Known as 'Bullshit' or 'BS' in American college culture. Called 'Cheat' in the UK and 'I Doubt It' in more formal settings. The game teaches bluffing and reading opponents.
history.evolution: The game exists in many variants with different rules for what ranks can be played, how many cards can be played, and challenge mechanics. The core bluffing element remains consistent.

rules.objective: Be the first player to get rid of all your cards by playing them to a central pile, either honestly or by bluffing about their rank.
rules.gameplay: The game begins with aces (or a chosen rank). The first player plays one or more cards face down, claiming they are aces. Play proceeds clockwise with next rank (2s, then 3s, etc.). After kings, it cycles back to aces. Players can play honestly or bluff. After any play, any other player can challenge by calling 'Bullshit!', 'Cheat!', or 'I Doubt It!'. The played cards are revealed. If the player was lying, they take the entire discard pile. If telling truth, the challenger takes the pile. The winner is first to empty their hand.
keyRules: Cards are played face down to a central pile
Players claim cards are of a specific rank (A, 2, 3...K, then back to A)
Can play 1-4 cards per turn (varies by variant)
Players can bluff (play cards of different rank than claimed)
Any player can challenge a play by calling 'Bullshit!', 'Cheat!', or 'I Doubt It!'
If bluffing: player takes the pile
If truthful: challenger takes the pile
Winner is first to empty their hand
Jokers may be wild (can represent any rank)

strategy.basic: Play honestly when possible to avoid getting caught. Challenge when you are certain someone is bluffing based on card counting. Don't challenge too often or you'll end up taking piles.
strategy.intermediate: Count cards to know what ranks have been played. Bluff strategically when you have many cards of a rank that has already passed. Watch opponents' patterns - some players always bluff on certain ranks.
strategy.advanced: Sophisticated bluffing patterns that are hard to read. Psychological manipulation through false tells. Optimal challenge timing based on probability and game state. Managing hand composition for endgame.
tips: Keep track of which ranks have been played
If you have all cards of a rank, you know others are bluffing
Don't challenge too frequently - only when confident
Mix honest plays with bluffs unpredictably
Save wild cards (jokers) for difficult ranks
Endgame strategy: play honestly when close to winning

scoring.description: First player to get rid of all their cards and survive any challenge resulting from their final play wins the deal. Tables that track scores across multiple deals can award one penalty point per card remaining in each loser’s hand when a deal ends.
